post.summary:
Retrieve AssetLldpNeighborXmedPoePd. AssetLldpNeighborXmedPoePd - This object describes the lldp neighbor MED POE PD info list.

Row classification:
A row is created for every AssetLldpNeighborXmed record (1:1 fan-out) regardless of
whether the neighbor advertised a MED Extended Power via MDI TLV (ANSI/TIA-1057 Section 10.2.5).
This means rows fall into two categories:

GENUINE PoE row: the neighbor sent an Extended Power TLV.
Indicated by: device_type IS NOT NULL AND power_source > 0.
These represent real powered or power-sourcing devices and should be
included in PoE analytics (count, by priority, by source).

PLACEHOLDER row: the neighbor is MED-capable but sent no PoE TLV.
Indicated by: device_type IS NULL AND power_source = 0.
These are hollow rows with no PoE meaning and should be EXCLUDED
from PoE analytics.

Knowledge graph filter rule:
Include as powered device:  device_type = 'PD_DEVICE'
Include as power source:    device_type = 'PSE_DEVICE'
Include with low confidence: device_type = 'UNKNOWN' AND power_source > 0
(PoE TLV received but type unresolvable; may be PD or PSE)
Exclude:                    device_type IS NULL OR power_source = 0

port.description:
Name of the interface, slot and port are required

	to ensure deterministic results, sub_port is optional.

	If the optional slot number for the management port is

	not provided on a stacked system, the slot will default

	to the master slot.

	[slot]:[port][:sub_port]

	'1:1:1'     slot=1, port=1, sub_port=1

	'12:101'    slot=12, port=101

	'1:s1'      insight port

	'ge2'       port=ge2

	'wifi1.3'   radio=1, ssid=3

	'mgmt'      oob mgmt port

	'2:mgmt'    mgmt port with optional slot

	'1:stack2'  stack port, slot=1, port=2

port_name.description: List of PortName. PortName represents State of the auto-sense on a port.

state.description: List of State. State represents State of the auto-sense on a port.

x-enum-descriptions: Unset (0): Valid zero value for unset state

DOWN (1): The port state transitions to the Auto-sense Down state when auto-sense is
attempted to enabled on disabled port or inactive link.

FA_PROXY_NO_AUTH (2): If the FA client switch does not use FA message authentication, the port
transitions to the FA PROXY NOAUTH state.

FA_PROXY (3): If LLDP detects an FA client switch that uses FA message authentication, the port
transitions to the FA PROXY state.

FA_WAP (4): The port enters the FA WAP state after LLDP detects an access point, an FA
client that is not another switch.
NO_AUTOSENSE (5): No Auto sense configured on port.

NNI (6): While the port is in the Wait state, if it receives a Fabric Connect LLDP packet,
the port transitions to the NNI state and adds the IS-IS SPBM instance on the interface.

NNI_ISIS_UP (7): The system tries to establish an IS-IS adjacency and, if successful, transitions
the port to the NNI IS-IS state.

NNI_LOOP (8): When a port is in the Auto-sense NNI state, if an already known system ID is
discovered through LLDP on a different port, the port transitions to the NNI loop state.
NNI_ONBOARDING (9): If the system cannot establish the adjacency, it transitions the port to the NNI onboarding state.
SD_WAN (11): After the first Auto-sense port receives an FE-TLV, the port transitions to the SD-WAN state.

SD_WAN_PENDING (12): All other Auto-sense ports not in SD-WAN state transition to SD-WAN-PENDING state and
remain unconfigured.

UNI_ONBOARDING (13): UNI_ONBOARDING state grants onboarding and data connectivity to the
port if you configure the onboarding I-SID or data I-SID in the global
Auto-sense configuration.
VOICE (14): If the port detects an LLDP packet from a phone, the port transitions to the VOICE state.

WAIT (15): The port state transitions to the Auto-sense Wait state after the port becomes
operational or the link becomes active.

wait_interval.description: List of WaitInterval. WaitInterval represents Timeout interval in seconds

x-enum-descriptions: Unset (0): Valid zero value for unset state

ALL802 (1): Includes all IEEE 802 Committee Address Family (aka Media Access Control (MAC) address)
plus Ethernet 'canonical format'.
AS_NUMBER (3): Autonomous System (AS) Number Address Family(16-bit quantity, per the AS number space).
BBN1822 (5): Bolt, Beranek, and Newman Report 1822 (BBN 1822) Address Family.
DEC_NET_4 (6): Digital Equipment DECnet Phase IV Address Family.
DISTINGUISHED_NAME (7): Distinguished Name, per X.500 Address Family.
DNS (8): Domain Name System (DNS) Address Family.
E164 (10): ITU-T E.164 (Switched Multimegabit Data Service (SMDS), Frame Relay, ATM) Address Family.
E164_NSAP (11): ITU-T E.164 with NSAP sub-address Address Family.
FIBRE_CHANNEL_WWPN (13): Fibre Channel (FC) World-Wide Port Name Address Family.
FIBRE_CHANNEL_WWNN (14): Fibre Channel (FC) World-Wide Node Name Address Family.
GW_ID (15): ATM Gateway Identifier (GWID) Number Address Family.
HDLC (16): High-Level Data Link Control (HDLC) Address Family (Characterized by 8-bit multidrop).
IPX (19): Novell Internetwork Packet Exchange (IPX) Address Family.
NSAP (20): OSI Network Service Access Point (NSAP) Address Family.
OTHER (21): None of the address families in this schema.
X121 (23): ITU-T X.121 (X.25, Frame Relay) Address Family.
XTP_NATIVE (24): XTP native mode Address Family.
XTP_OVER_IPV4 (25): Xpress Transport Protocol (XTP) over Ipv4 Address Family.
XTP_OVER_IPV6 (26): Xpress Transport Protocol (XTP) over Ipv6 Address Family.

x-enum-descriptions: Unset (0): Valid zero value for unset state

CHASSIS_COMPONENT (1): Chassis identifier based on the value of entPhysicalAlias
object defined in IETF RFC 2737.

INTERFACE_ALIAS (2): Chassis identifier based on the value of ifAlias object
defined in IETF RFC 2863.

INTERFACE_NAME (3): Chassis identifier based on the name of the interface,
e.g., the value of ifName object defined in IETF RFC 2863.
LOCAL (4): Chassis identifier based on a locally defined value.

PORT_COMPONENT (5): Chassis identifier based on the value of entPhysicalAlias
object defined in IETF RFC 2737 for a port or backplane component.

MAC_ADDRESS (6): Chassis identifier based on the value of a unicast source
address (encoded in network byte order and IEEE 802.3 canonical bit order), of a
port on the containing chassis as defined in IEEE Std 802-2001.

NETWORK_ADDRESS (7): Chassis identifier based on a network address, associated with
a particular chassis.  The encoded address is composed of two fields.
The first field is a single octet, representing the IANA AddressFamilyNumbers
value for the specific address type, and the second field is
the network address value.

admin_status.description: List of AdminStatus. AdminStatus represents Device administrative status. UP, DOWN, TESTING and RESET are applicable to Fabric Engine, ENABLED is applicable to Switch Engine.

x-enum-descriptions: Unset (0): Valid zero value for unset state
UP (1): Device admin state up and passing packets.
TESTING (3): Device admin state is set to test.
RESET (4): Device admin state is set to reset.
ENABLED (5): Device admin state is set to enabled state. ENABLED is applicable to Switch Engine.

chassis_id.description:
List of ChassisId. ChassisId represents The string value used to identify the chassis component
	associated with the local system as described by IEEE 802.1AB-2005 9.5.2.3.

chassis_id_subtype.description: List of ChassisIdSubtype. ChassisIdSubtype represents The type of encoding used to identify the chassis associated with the local system as described by IEEE 802.1AB-2005 9.5.2.2.

x-enum-descriptions: Unset (0): Valid zero value for unset state

CHASSIS_COMPONENT (1): Chassis identifier based on the value of entPhysicalAlias
object defined in IETF RFC 2737.

INTERFACE_ALIAS (2): Chassis identifier based on the value of ifAlias object
defined in IETF RFC 2863.

INTERFACE_NAME (3): Chassis identifier based on the name of the interface,
e.g., the value of ifName object defined in IETF RFC 2863.
LOCAL (4): Chassis identifier based on a locally defined value.

PORT_COMPONENT (5): Chassis identifier based on the value of entPhysicalAlias
object defined in IETF RFC 2737 for a port or backplane component.

MAC_ADDRESS (6): Chassis identifier based on the value of a unicast source
address (encoded in network byte order and IEEE 802.3 canonical bit order), of a
port on the containing chassis as defined in IEEE Std 802-2001.

NETWORK_ADDRESS (7): Chassis identifier based on a network address, associated with
a particular chassis.  The encoded address is composed of two fields.
The first field is a single octet, representing the IANA AddressFamilyNumbers
value for the specific address type, and the second field is
the network address value.

operation_status.description:
List of OperationStatus. OperationStatus represents Device operational status indicating the current operational state of the device.
	Values: UP, DOWN, TESTING, UNKNOWN, DORMANT, UP_MASTER, UP_DORMANT, UP_WARMSTANDBY,
	EMPTY, PRESENT, FAILED, POWEROFF, POWEREDOFF, MISMATCH, POWERON, POWERON_DONE,
	EPOST, EPOST_DONE, DOWNLOADING, DOWNLOADED, BOOTING, BOOTING_DONE, DIAG, DIAG_DONE,
	OFFLINING, OFFLINE, INIT, INIT_DONE, VLAN_SYNC, VLAN_SYNCED, FDB_SYNC, FDB_SYNCED,
	ACL_SYNC, ACL_SYNCED, RT_SYNC, RT_SYNCED, OPERATIONAL, REBOOTING.

x-enum-descriptions: Unset (0): Valid zero value for unset state
UP (1): Device ready to pass packets.
DOWN (2): The device does not pass any packets.
TESTING (3): In some test mode. No operational packets can be passed.
UNKNOWN (4): Status cannot be determined for some reason.
DORMANT (5): Device is in dormant state. Waiting for some external event.
UP_MASTER (6): Device operation state up and master.
UP_DORMANT (7): Device operation state up and in dormant state.
UP_WARMSTANDBY (8): Device operation state up and in in standby mode as its warm.
EMPTY (9): Device operation state is empty.
POWEROFF (12): Device is in power off state.
POWEREDOFF (13): Device operation state powered off.
POWERON (15): Device operation state power on.
POWERON_DONE (16): Device operation state power on done.
EPOST (17): Device operation state power on epost.
EPOST_DONE (18): Device operation state power on epost done.
DOWNLOADED (20): Device operation state downloading done.
BOOTING_DONE (22): Device operation state booting done.
DIAG_DONE (24): Device operation state diagnostic done.
OFFLINE (26): Device operation state offline done.
INIT_DONE (28): Device operation state init done.
VLAN_SYNC (29): Device operation state vlan sync.
VLAN_SYNCED (30): Device operation state vlan sync done.
FDB_SYNC (31): Device operation state fdb sync.
FDB_SYNCED (32): Device operation state fdb sync done.
ACL_SYNC (33): Device operation state acl sync.
ACL_SYNCED (34): Device operation state acl sync done.
RT_SYNC (35): Device operation state rt sync.
RT_SYNCED (36): Device operation state rt sync done.

operation_status.description:
Device operational status indicating the current operational state of the device.
	Values: UP, DOWN, TESTING, UNKNOWN, DORMANT, UP_MASTER, UP_DORMANT, UP_WARMSTANDBY,
	EMPTY, PRESENT, FAILED, POWEROFF, POWEREDOFF, MISMATCH, POWERON, POWERON_DONE,
	EPOST, EPOST_DONE, DOWNLOADING, DOWNLOADED, BOOTING, BOOTING_DONE, DIAG, DIAG_DONE,

	ACL_SYNC, ACL_SYNCED, RT_SYNC, RT_SYNCED, OPERATIONAL, REBOOTING.

UP (1): Device ready to pass packets.
DOWN (2): The device does not pass any packets.
TESTING (3): In some test mode. No operational packets can be passed.
UNKNOWN (4): Status cannot be determined for some reason.
DORMANT (5): Device is in dormant state. Waiting for some external event.
UP_MASTER (6): Device operation state up and master.
UP_DORMANT (7): Device operation state up and in dormant state.
UP_WARMSTANDBY (8): Device operation state up and in in standby mode as its warm.
EMPTY (9): Device operation state is empty.
POWEROFF (12): Device is in power off state.
POWEREDOFF (13): Device operation state powered off.
POWERON (15): Device operation state power on.
POWERON_DONE (16): Device operation state power on done.
EPOST (17): Device operation state power on epost.
EPOST_DONE (18): Device operation state power on epost done.
DOWNLOADED (20): Device operation state downloading done.
BOOTING_DONE (22): Device operation state booting done.
DIAG_DONE (24): Device operation state diagnostic done.
OFFLINE (26): Device operation state offline done.
INIT_DONE (28): Device operation state init done.
VLAN_SYNC (29): Device operation state vlan sync.
VLAN_SYNCED (30): Device operation state vlan sync done.
FDB_SYNC (31): Device operation state fdb sync.
FDB_SYNCED (32): Device operation state fdb sync done.
ACL_SYNC (33): Device operation state acl sync.
ACL_SYNCED (34): Device operation state acl sync done.
RT_SYNC (35): Device operation state rt sync.
RT_SYNCED (36): Device operation state rt sync done.
Unset (0): Valid zero value for unset state
TPME_OS (5): OS type TPME (Third Party Management Engine).
TPME_MANAGED_DEVICE_OS (6): OS type TPME (Third Party Management Engine) Managed Device.

admin_status.description: Device administrative status. UP, DOWN, TESTING and RESET are applicable to Fabric Engine, ENABLED is applicable to Switch Engine.
x-enum-descriptions: Unset (0): Valid zero value for unset state
UP (1): Device admin state up and passing packets.
TESTING (3): Device admin state is set to test.
RESET (4): Device admin state is set to reset.
ENABLED (5): Device admin state is set to enabled state. ENABLED is applicable to Switch Engine.

chassis_id.description:
The string value used to identify the chassis component
	associated with the local system as described by IEEE 802.1AB-2005 9.5.2.3.

chassis_id_subtype.description: The type of encoding used to identify the chassis associated with the local system as described by IEEE 802.1AB-2005 9.5.2.2.
x-enum-descriptions: Unset (0): Valid zero value for unset state

CHASSIS_COMPONENT (1): Chassis identifier based on the value of entPhysicalAlias
object defined in IETF RFC 2737.

INTERFACE_ALIAS (2): Chassis identifier based on the value of ifAlias object
defined in IETF RFC 2863.

INTERFACE_NAME (3): Chassis identifier based on the name of the interface,
e.g., the value of ifName object defined in IETF RFC 2863.
LOCAL (4): Chassis identifier based on a locally defined value.

PORT_COMPONENT (5): Chassis identifier based on the value of entPhysicalAlias
object defined in IETF RFC 2737 for a port or backplane component.

MAC_ADDRESS (6): Chassis identifier based on the value of a unicast source
address (encoded in network byte order and IEEE 802.3 canonical bit order), of a
port on the containing chassis as defined in IEEE Std 802-2001.

NETWORK_ADDRESS (7): Chassis identifier based on a network address, associated with
a particular chassis.  The encoded address is composed of two fields.
The first field is a single octet, representing the IANA AddressFamilyNumbers
value for the specific address type, and the second field is
the network address value.

assignment_timeout.description: Fabric Attach assignment timeout in seconds. For Switch Engine it is a read only attribute.

created_at.description: Specifies the date and time when the entry was created.

discovery_timeout.description: Fabric Attach discovery timeout in seconds. This setting applies to Fabric Engine only.

enabled.description:
Indicates whether the Fabric Attach service is active on the device. On Switch
	Engine, this setting is read only. Note that the forwarding field is independent
	of enabled — forwarding may be false even when enabled is true.

forwarding.description:
When set to true, Fabric Attach Proxy switches send management VLAN data to clients.
	This field is independent of the enabled field — a device may have enabled set to
	true while forwarding remains false. This setting applies to Switch Engine only.

id.description: An auto-generated primary key identifier of the table in the UUID format defined in RFC 4122.

mgmt_vlan.description:
The VLAN advertised to fabric attach clients for them to use
	as the management VLAN. Value set to 0 is a sentinel meaning that no management
	VLAN is configured. Value set to 4095 indicates that Management
	traffic should be sent untagged. This setting applies
	to Switch Engine only.

updated_at.description: Specifies the date and time when the entry was last updated.

uplink_port.description:
The uplink port name for standalone proxy operation. Name of the interface, slot and port are required to ensure deterministic results, sub_port is optional. This definition allows for the string 'None' to unconfigure the uplink port. Switch Engine only.

	 [slot]:[port][:sub_port]
	'1:1:1'    slot=1, port=1, sub_port=1
	'12:101'   slot=12, port=101

AssetFabricAttachConfig.description:
AssetFabricAttachConfig - DB Model for Fabric Attach configuration settings per device.

Consumers should use the standalone endpoints for cross-device

authentication_key.description:
Provides access to the Fabric Attach  message authentication key
	for the associated interface. Switch Engine allows configuration
	of both cleartext and encrypted keys. The maximum length for
	configuration of a cleartext key is 32 characters. For Switch
	Engine this corresponds to a maximum encrypted length of 110
	characters.

created_at.description: Specifies the date and time when the entry was created.

enabled.description: Status of Fabric Attach on a port.

fabric_attach_config_id.description: This object represents the fabric attach settings for a port.

forwarding.description:
When set to true, Fabric Attach Proxy switches send management VLAN data to clients.
	This field is independent of the enabled field — a device may have enabled set to
	true while forwarding remains false. This setting applies to Switch Engine only.

id.description: An auto-generated primary key identifier of the table in the UUID format defined in RFC 4122.

key_encrypted.description:
A value of true indicates that key encryption is enabled for
	the associated interface. This field is independent of
	message-authentication-enabled — it is valid and expected for
	message-authentication-enabled to be true while key-encrypted is false,
	meaning authentication is active but keys are stored in cleartext.
	This setting applies to Switch Engine only.

key_rotated.description: The flag to indicate if the key is rotated.

message_authentication_enabled.description:
Status of the Fabric Attach message authentication for the associated interface.
	When true, FA packets are authenticated. Note that key-encrypted may still be false
	even when this is true, indicating authentication is active with unencrypted keys.
	See key-encrypted for the encryption state of the authentication key.

mgmt_cvid.description:
Fabric Attach management customer vid for the associated interface.
	A value of 0 is a sentinel meaning the management i-sid feature is not
	enabled; consumers should treat 0 as equivalent to null/absent.
	4095 is not used. 4096 is reserved for the untagged case.
	This setting applies to Fabric Engine only.

mgmt_nsi.description:
Fabric Attach management network service (i-sid) id
	for the associated interface. A value of 0 is a sentinel meaning the
	management i-sid feature is not enabled; consumers should treat 0 as
	equivalent to null/absent. Values of 16000000 and greater are reserved
	for internal use. This setting applies to Fabric Engine only.

origin.description:
Indicates how the Fabric Attach interface was configured on the port.
	CONFIG indicates the interface was configured manually via CLI or SNMP.
	AUTO_SENSE indicates the interface was configured automatically via
	Zero Touch Fabric (ZTF). Ports with AUTO_SENSE origin are typically
	the same ports where enabled is true. This setting applies to Fabric Engine only.

forwarding.description:
When set to true, Fabric Attach Proxy switches send management VLAN data to clients.
	This field is independent of the enabled field — a device may have enabled set to
	true while forwarding remains false. This setting applies to Switch Engine only.

key_encrypted.description:
A value of true indicates that key encryption is enabled for
	the associated interface. This field is independent of
	message-authentication-enabled — it is valid and expected for
	message-authentication-enabled to be true while key-encrypted is false,
	meaning authentication is active but keys are stored in cleartext.
	This setting applies to Switch Engine only.

key_rotated.description: The flag to indicate if the key is rotated.

message_authentication_enabled.description:
Status of the Fabric Attach message authentication for the associated interface.
	When true, FA packets are authenticated. Note that key-encrypted may still be false
	even when this is true, indicating authentication is active with unencrypted keys.
	See key-encrypted for the encryption state of the authentication key.

mgmt_cvid.description:

	A value of 0 is a sentinel meaning the management i-sid feature is not
	enabled; consumers should treat 0 as equivalent to null/absent.
	4095 is not used. 4096 is reserved for the untagged case.
	This setting applies to Fabric Engine only.

mgmt_nsi.description:
Fabric Attach management network service (i-sid) id
	for the associated interface. A value of 0 is a sentinel meaning the
	management i-sid feature is not enabled; consumers should treat 0 as
	equivalent to null/absent. Values of 16000000 and greater are reserved
	for internal use. This setting applies to Fabric Engine only.

origin.description:

	CONFIG indicates the interface was configured manually via CLI or SNMP.
	AUTO_SENSE indicates the interface was configured automatically via
	Zero Touch Fabric (ZTF). Ports with AUTO_SENSE origin are typically
	the same ports where enabled is true. This setting applies to Fabric Engine only.

DIAG_DONE (24): Device operation state diagnostic done.

VLAN_SYNC (29): Device operation state vlan sync.
VLAN_SYNCED (30): Device operation state vlan sync done.

ACL_SYNC (33): Device operation state acl sync.

allow_dynamic.description:
A value of true indicates that this port is statically added as a tagged uplink port
	to all dynamically created VLAN's. This property only applies to Switch Engine.

asset_interface_id.description:
UUID of the AssetInterface record (extreme-asset-interface) for this port.
	Follow this reference to obtain interface-type, interface-name, and the
	owning device (asset-device-id).

created_at.description: Specifies the date and time when the entry was created.

interface_name.description: Interface name. Maximum length: 64 characters.

interface_type.description: The type of interface.

is_brouter.description: A value of true indicates this port is part of a BROUTER type VLAN. This is VOSS specific.

port_type.description:
The port type (ACCESS or TRUNK). An access port can not be assigned to a VLAN as tagged.
	For VOSS, tagging can be enabled on the port which sets it as a trunk port.  For EXOS,
	there is no explicit configuration of a trunk port so this setting can be set to trunk
	or set to access if the port is not assigned to a VLAN as tagged.
	Values: 0=Unset, 1=ACCESS, 2=TRUNK, 3=AUTOSENSE, 4=GENERAL, 5=FABRICTRUNK, 6=BACKHAUL.

port_vlan.description:
Untagged packets received on this port are assigned to the VLAN specified by this property. A value of 0,
	is used to unset this parameter.

pvlan.description:
The private vlan setting for the port. This is a Fabric Engine
	specific setting. Values: 0=Unset, 1=NONE, 2=ISOLATED, 3=PROMISCUOUS, 4=TRUNK.

spb_mcast_enabled.description:
A value of true indicates that this port is SPB Multicast enabled.
	This is a Fabric Engine specific setting.

untagged_egress.description:
A value of true indicates that this port will transmit the portVlan as untagged on a
	trunk port. This is a Fabric Engine specific setting.

is_brouter.description: List of IsBrouter. IsBrouter represents A value of true indicates this port is part of a BROUTER type VLAN. This is VOSS specific.

port_type.description:
List of PortType. PortType represents The port type (ACCESS or TRUNK). An access port can not be assigned to a VLAN as tagged.
	For VOSS, tagging can be enabled on the port which sets it as a trunk port.  For EXOS,
	there is no explicit configuration of a trunk port so this setting can be set to trunk
	or set to access if the port is not assigned to a VLAN as tagged.
	Values: 0=Unset, 1=ACCESS, 2=TRUNK, 3=AUTOSENSE, 4=GENERAL, 5=FABRICTRUNK, 6=BACKHAUL.

x-enum-descriptions: Unset (0): Valid zero value for unset state

ACCESS (1): An access port can have only one VLAN configured on the interface; it can
carry traffic for only one VLAN.
For wireless interface, this mode refers to Bridge-access mode.

TRUNK (2): A trunk port can have two or more VLANs configured on the interface; it can carry
traffic for several VLANs simultaneously
For wireless interface, this mode refers to Bridge-802.Q1 mode.

AUTOSENSE (3): An Autosense port automatically detect and adjust to the speed and characteristics
of the connected devices

GENERAL (4): Ports are endpoints in network communication, categorized into well-known,
registered, and dynamic/private types for efficient data transfer.

BACKHAUL (6): Set the interface in backhaul mode, making it a VLAN-aware layer 2 interface through which the default
MAC route for traffic to and from the main LAN passes.
Applicable only for wireless devices.

port_vlan.description:
List of PortVlan. PortVlan represents Untagged packets received on this port are assigned to the VLAN specified by this property. A value of 0,
	is used to unset this parameter.

pvlan.description:
List of Pvlan. Pvlan represents The private vlan setting for the port. This is a Fabric Engine
	specific setting. Values: 0=Unset, 1=NONE, 2=ISOLATED, 3=PROMISCUOUS, 4=TRUNK.

x-enum-descriptions: Unset (0): Valid zero value for unset state

ISOLATED (2): Carries traffic from isolated ports. Isolated ports can communicate only with the
promiscuous ports of the same PVLAN.

PROMISCUOUS (3): A port that can communicate with all other PVLAN ports, including
external routers, network management devices and administrative workstations.

TRUNK (4): A port that is a member of all VLANs within the PVLAN, and can communicate
with all ports. This enables tagging.

spb_mcast_enabled.description:
List of SpbMcastEnabled. SpbMcastEnabled represents A value of true indicates that this port is SPB Multicast enabled.
	This is a Fabric Engine specific setting.

untagged_egress.description:
List of UntaggedEgress. UntaggedEgress represents A value of true indicates that this port will transmit the portVlan as untagged on a
	trunk port. This is a Fabric Engine specific setting.

cvid.description:
Used to identify customer vid of the switched uni port that
	this entry is associated with. 0 means there is no switched uni association.
	4095 is not used. 4096 is a sentinel value meaning 'all VLANs' (untagged case).
	Valid VLAN ID range is 1..4094.
	This attribute applies to Fabric Engine only.

id.description: An auto-generated primary key identifier of the table in the UUID format defined in RFC 4122.

interface_name.description:
Either the value 0, or the port name or associated LAG ID
	of the port on which a frame having a source address equal to the
	value of the corresponding MAC addrress has been seen.
	A value of 0 indicates that the port number has not been
	learned but that the bridge does have some forwarding/filtering
	information about this address.
	A value of 'cpp' indicates a self-assigned MAC address.

interface_type.description:
This attribute indicates the interface type on which the MAC
	is learnt. LAG type is applicable for Fabric Engine only.
	Integer values: 1=ETHERNET, 2=LAG, 3=UNKNOWN

is_id.description:
A value that uniquely identifies the Layer 2 and Layer 3 services instances network-wide.
	Values greater than 16000000 are for Layer 2 instances dynamically added. For set operations,
	the ISID maximum value is 15999999.

mac_address.description:
A unicast MAC address for which the bridge has
	forwarding and/or filtering information.

origin.description:
This attribute indicates whether the MAC address was
	learned locally or on NNI port from a remote destination.

remote_mac_bvlan_id.description:
The value indicates the backbone VLAN ID for this MAC address
	if it is learned remotely. Otherwise a value of 0 is displayed.

remote_mac_destination_address.description:
A provider MAC address for which the bridge has forwarding
	and/or filtering information. This value is displayed only if the port
	type is remote otherwise a value of 0 is displayed.

remote_mac_destination_system_name.description:
Primary system name of the node where MAC address entry was
	learned from in case of remote otherwise NULL is shown.

status.description:
This attribute indicates the status of the Forwarding
	Database entry. This attribute applies to Fabric Engine only.
	Integer values: 1=INVALID, 2=LEARNED, 3=MGMT, 4=OTHER, 5=SELF, 6=ANYCAST

updated_at.description: Specifies the date and time when the entry was last updated.

The port name indicates which of the bridge's ports has this
address.

ANYCAST (6): static anycast MAC entry.
The port name indicates which of the bridge's ports has this
address.

area_name.description:
The ISIS system area-name. This attribute is available in both areas
	and if the device does not support multi-area, it won`t be included
	in the home response. An empty string indicates no area name is
	configured; consumers should treat an empty string as equivalent to
	null/absent.

area_type.description:
ISIS area type for this adjacency.
	Known enum values:
	1 = HOME — the local ISIS area;
	2 = REMOTE — a remote ISIS area.

created_at.description: Specifies the date and time when the entry was created.

hold_timer.description: The hold time in seconds for this adjacency. Valid range: 1..65535 seconds.

host_name.description:
The hostname listed in LSP or the system name if host
	name is not configured.

id.description: An auto-generated primary key identifier of the table in the UUID format defined in RFC 4122.

interface_name.description: The name of the interface to which the circuit corresponds.

last_up_time.description:
Time elapsed in centiseconds (hundredths of a second) since the adjacency
	most recently entered the state 'up'. Minimum value is 0 (adjacency just
	transitioned to UP). A value of 0 also indicates the adjacency has not yet
	been UP.

neighbor_priority.description:
Priority of the neighboring Intermediate System for
	becoming the Designated Intermediate System..

neighbor_sys_id.description: The system ID of the neighboring Intermediate System.

parallel_active_flag.description:
A flag to indicate current adjacency is active or not
	among all the parallel adjacencies between two nodes.

updated_at.description: Specifies the date and time when the entry was last updated.

	Known values: IPV4, IPV6.

created_at.description: Specifies the date and time when the entry was created.

enabled.description: A value of True enables the redistribution of the specified protocol into the ISIS network.

isid.description:
A value that uniquely identifies the Layer 2 and Layer 3 service instances network-wide.
	Valid range: 1..16777215 (24-bit ISID space). Valid user-configurable range is 1 to 15999999.
	Values of 16000000 and greater are reserved for Layer 2 instances dynamically added by

metric.description:

	Valid range: 1..16777215.

metric_type.description:
Specifies the type of route to import from the protocol.
	Known values: INTERNAL, EXTERNAL.

protocol.description:
Specifies the protocol from which the routes are redistributed in ISIS.
	Known values include: DIRECT, STATIC, OSPF, BGP, RIP.

route_policy.description: Configures the route policy to apply the redistributes routes. Maximum length: 64 characters.

subnets.description:
Indicates whether the subnets are advertised individually or aggregated
	to their classful subnet. Applicable to IPv4 redistribution only.
	Known values: ALLOW (subnets advertised individually),
	SUPPRESS (subnets aggregated to classful boundary),
	NONE (no subnet advertisement configuration).

updated_at.description: Specifies the date and time when the entry was last updated.

ISID. A value that uniquely identifies the Layer 2 and Layer 3 services instances network-wide.
	Values greater than 16000000 are for Layer 2 instances dynamically added. For set operations,
	the ISID maximum value is 15999999. Note: this field is named is-id (JSON: is_id) in this model;
	other ISIS models use isid (no underscore) for the same concept — consumers must account for
	this naming inconsistency when building cross-model queries. some other models also use i-sid.

is_id_name.description:
A value that uniquely identifies the ISID.  is-id-name also could be know as i-sid-name.
	Note the fan-iSID is the Fabric Attach Network I-SID - a special, automatically assigned service
	instance identifier used by Fabric Attach (FA) to map non-SPBM edge devices
	(like EXOS switches, WLAN APs, or IP phones) into the SPBM fabric.
	It is not a user-configured service I-SID; instead, it is dynamically signaled by the FA
	client and used by the BEB to place that device into the correct virtual service.

AssetIsisMulticastFibState.description:
AssetIsisMulticastFibState - The object that represents state of SPBM IP Multicast-FIB entries.
The response embeds multicast-fib-interface records as two nested arrays:
incoming_interface (single entry) and outgoing_interfaces (array of entries).
To query which ports carry a specific ISID's multicast traffic, consumers
must filter or UNNEST the outgoing_interfaces array. IncomingInterface,OutgoingInterfaces can be created while creating AssetIsisMulticastFibState.

	IP multicast data from a sender, it auto-allocates a data I-SID in the
	range 16,000,000 to 16,512,000 for the stream. The stream is identified by

advertisement_interval.description:
The advertisement interval determines how frequently LLDP-enabled devices send
	advertisement frames to their neighbors.
	For Wired devices, the default interval is 30 seconds.
	For Wireless devices, the default interval is 90 seconds.

	For Wired device, a valid interval must be in range: 5-32768
	For Wireless device, a valid interval must be in range: 5-65534

created_at.description: Specifies the date and time when the entry was created.

enabled.description: Enable or disable LLDP functionality on the device.

fabric_attach.description:
Enable or disable LLDP Fabric Attach functionality on the device. Fabric Attach is an
	extension to LLDP that provides automatic provisioning of network services and policies - Not supported on Wired devices

fast_start_repeat_count.description:
The fast-start-repeat-count specifies how many times LLDP Media Endpoint Discovery
	(LLDP-MED) packets are sent at 1-second intervals when a new LLDP-MED device is detected.
	This helps the device quickly learn about its neighbors. The range is from 1 to 10, with a
	default value of 3 - Not supported on Wireless devices

hold_multiplier.description:
The hold multiplier determines how long the information about a device is retained by its
	neighbors. It is a multiplier applied to the advertisement interval to calculate the
	Time-to-Live (TTL) for the LLDP data. By default, the hold multiplier is set to 4, but it
	can be configured to range from 2 to 10 - Not supported on Wireless devices

holdtime.description:
The hold time value in seconds that specifies how long LLDP information should be
	retained by receiving devices - Not supported on Wired devices.

	For wireless devices, the default holdtime is 90 seconds.

id.description: An auto-generated primary key identifier of the table in the UUID format defined in RFC 4122.

init_delay_seconds.description:
The initialization delay (init delay) specifies the minimum number of seconds a device
	will wait after LLDP is disabled on a port before it will re-enable LLDP on that port. The
	default value for this delay is 2 seconds, but it can typically be configured to range
	from 1 to 10 seconds - Not supported on Wireless devices

max_entries.description:
Maximum number of LLDP neighbor entries to store - Not supported on Wired devices

	For wireless devices, the default max-entries is 64.

max_power.description:
Maximum power requested in units of 0.1 watts. A value of 255 represents 25.5 watts - Not supported on Wired devices.

	For wireless devices, the default max-power is 255 (25.5 watts).

receive_only.description:
Enable receive-only mode where the device will only receive LLDP packets but will not
	transmit LLDP advertisements - Not supported on Wired devices

	For wireless devices, the default value is false.

updated_at.description: Specifies the date and time when the entry was last updated.

	Value is defined by IEEE 802.1AB-2005 9.5.9.4.

address_subtype.description:
List of AddressSubtype. AddressSubtype represents  IANA address family number identifying the address type of the management address.
	Values: 0=Unset, 1=ALL_802, 2=APPLE_TALK, 3=AS_NUMBER, 4=BANYAN_VINES, 5=BBN1822, 6=DEC_NET4, 7=DISTINGUISHED_NAME, 8=DNS, 9=E163, 10=E164, 11=E164_NSAP, 12=F69, 13=FIBRE_CHANNEL_WWPN, 14=FIBRE_CHANNEL_WWNN, 15=GW_ID, 16=HDLC, 17=IPv4, 18=IPv6, 19=IPX, 20=NSAP, 21=OTHER, 22=RESERVED, 23=X121, 24=XTP_NATIVE, 25=XTP_OVER_IPV4, 26=XTP_OVER_IPV6.

x-enum-descriptions: Unset (0): Valid zero value for unset state

ALL802 (1): Includes all IEEE 802 Committee Address Family (aka Media Access Control (MAC) address)
plus Ethernet 'canonical format'.
AS_NUMBER (3): Autonomous System (AS) Number Address Family(16-bit quantity, per the AS number space).
BBN1822 (5): Bolt, Beranek, and Newman Report 1822 (BBN 1822) Address Family.
DEC_NET_4 (6): Digital Equipment DECnet Phase IV Address Family.
DISTINGUISHED_NAME (7): Distinguished Name, per X.500 Address Family.
DNS (8): Domain Name System (DNS) Address Family.
E164 (10): ITU-T E.164 (Switched Multimegabit Data Service (SMDS), Frame Relay, ATM) Address Family.
E164_NSAP (11): ITU-T E.164 with NSAP sub-address Address Family.
FIBRE_CHANNEL_WWPN (13): Fibre Channel (FC) World-Wide Port Name Address Family.
FIBRE_CHANNEL_WWNN (14): Fibre Channel (FC) World-Wide Node Name Address Family.
GW_ID (15): ATM Gateway Identifier (GWID) Number Address Family.
HDLC (16): High-Level Data Link Control (HDLC) Address Family (Characterized by 8-bit multidrop).
IPX (19): Novell Internetwork Packet Exchange (IPX) Address Family.
NSAP (20): OSI Network Service Access Point (NSAP) Address Family.
OTHER (21): None of the address families in this schema.
X121 (23): ITU-T X.121 (X.25, Frame Relay) Address Family.
XTP_NATIVE (24): XTP native mode Address Family.
XTP_OVER_IPV4 (25): Xpress Transport Protocol (XTP) over Ipv4 Address Family.
XTP_OVER_IPV6 (26): Xpress Transport Protocol (XTP) over Ipv6 Address Family.

	This is used by control mechanism that prevents over current situations by
	disconnecting first ports with lower power priority.
	CRITICAL - power priority is critical, as per RFC 3621
	HIGH     - power priority is high, as per RFC 3621

power_type.description:
The Power Type value.
	Indicates specific wiring configuration used for power transmission.

	Mode A: Power is delivered over the same wire pairs used for data transmission in 10BASE-T and 100BASE-TX Ethernet (pins 1-2 and 3-6).
	Mode B: Power is delivered over the 'spare' wire pairs (pins 4-5 and 7-8).
	Mode A and B (4-Pair): Both sets of pairs are used simultaneously to provide higher power.

	TYPE_1   - Can use either Mode A or Mode B. Can provide up to 15.4W of power.
	TYPE_2   - Can use either Mode A or Mode B. Can provide up to 30W of power.
	TYPE_3   - Can use both Mode A and B at the same time. Can provide up to 60W of power.
	TYPE_4   - Can use both Mode A and B at the same time. Can provide up to 90W of power.

AssetLldpNeighborXmedPoePd.description:
AssetLldpNeighborXmedPoePd - This object describes the lldp neighbor MED POE PD info list.

Row classification:
A row is created for every AssetLldpNeighborXmed record (1:1 fan-out) regardless of
whether the neighbor advertised a MED Extended Power via MDI TLV (ANSI/TIA-1057 Section 10.2.5).
This means rows fall into two categories:

GENUINE PoE row: the neighbor sent an Extended Power TLV.
Indicated by: device_type IS NOT NULL AND power_source > 0.
These represent real powered or power-sourcing devices and should be
included in PoE analytics (count, by priority, by source).

PLACEHOLDER row: the neighbor is MED-capable but sent no PoE TLV.
Indicated by: device_type IS NULL AND power_source = 0.
These are hollow rows with no PoE meaning and should be EXCLUDED
from PoE analytics.

Knowledge graph filter rule:
Include as powered device:  device_type = 'PD_DEVICE'
Include as power source:    device_type = 'PSE_DEVICE'
Include with low confidence: device_type = 'UNKNOWN' AND power_source > 0
(PoE TLV received but type unresolvable; may be PD or PSE)
Exclude:                    device_type IS NULL OR power_source = 0

AssetLldpNeighborXmedPoePdGetResponse.description:
AssetLldpNeighborXmedPoePdGetResponse represents a single AssetLldpNeighborXmedPoePd response. AssetLldpNeighborXmedPoePd - This object describes the lldp neighbor MED POE PD info list.

Row classification:
A row is created for every AssetLldpNeighborXmed record (1:1 fan-out) regardless of
whether the neighbor advertised a MED Extended Power via MDI TLV (ANSI/TIA-1057 Section 10.2.5).
This means rows fall into two categories:

GENUINE PoE row: the neighbor sent an Extended Power TLV.
Indicated by: device_type IS NOT NULL AND power_source > 0.
These represent real powered or power-sourcing devices and should be
included in PoE analytics (count, by priority, by source).

PLACEHOLDER row: the neighbor is MED-capable but sent no PoE TLV.
Indicated by: device_type IS NULL AND power_source = 0.
These are hollow rows with no PoE meaning and should be EXCLUDED
from PoE analytics.

Knowledge graph filter rule:
Include as powered device:  device_type = 'PD_DEVICE'
Include as power source:    device_type = 'PSE_DEVICE'
Include with low confidence: device_type = 'UNKNOWN' AND power_source > 0
(PoE TLV received but type unresolvable; may be PD or PSE)
Exclude:                    device_type IS NULL OR power_source = 0

device_type.description:

	Per ANSI/TIA-1057, Section 10.2.5.1.

	Values:
	   NONE       - TLV received but no device type was set. Exclude from PoE analytics.
	   PD_DEVICE  - Device is a Powered Device (draws power from a PSE). Definitive PoE device.
	   PSE_DEVICE - Device is Power Sourcing Equipment (provides power). Definitive power source.
	   UNKNOWN    - A MED Extended Power TLV was received but the device type was unresolvable.
	                The neighbor IS a PoE participant but its role (PD or PSE) cannot be determined.
	                Distinguish from NULL using power_source: if power_source > 0 then UNKNOWN
	                means 'TLV received, type unclear'; if power_source = 0 then treat as NULL.

	NULL semantics:
	   NULL means no MED Extended Power TLV was received from this neighbor at all.
	   This row is a placeholder created by the 1:1 fan-out from AssetLldpNeighborXmed.
	   NULL device_type combined with power_source = 0 is the definitive hollow-row signal
	   and should be excluded from all PoE analytics.

	Key distinction:
	   UNKNOWN + power_source > 0  = PoE TLV received, role unknown  (include with low confidence)
	   UNKNOWN + power_source = 0  = treat same as NULL               (exclude)
	   NONE    + any               = TLV received, no type set        (exclude)
	   NULL    + power_source = 0  = no PoE TLV, hollow placeholder   (exclude)

	with the remote system connected at given port. Valid range is 0-7.
	For details see ANSI/TIA-1057, Section 10.2.3.6.
	IEEE 802.1p PCP values:
	0 = BK (Background, priority 1 - lowest)
	1 = BE (Best Effort, priority 0 - default)
	2 = EE (Excellent Effort, priority 2)
	3 = CA (Critical Applications, priority 3)
	4 = VI (Video, < 100ms latency and jitter, priority 4)
	5 = VO (Voice, < 10ms latency and jitter, priority 5)
	6 = IC (Internetwork Control, priority 6)
	7 = NC (Network Control, priority 7 - highest).

tagged_enabled.description:
A value of 'true' indicates that the application is using a tagged VLAN.
	A value of 'false' indicates that for the specific application the device either is
	using an untagged VLAN or does not support port based VLAN operation. In this case,
	both the vlanId and priority attributes are ignored and only the DSCP value has relevance.
	For details see ANSI/TIA-1057, Section 10.2.3.3.

updated_at.description: Specifies the date and time when the entry was last updated.

vlan_id.description:
An extension of the VLAN Identifier for the remote system connected to
	this port, as defined in IEEE 802.1P-1998. A value of 1 through 4094 is used
	to define a valid PVID. A value of 0 shall be used if the device is using
	priority tagged frames, meaning that only the 802.1p priority level is significant
	and the default VID of the ingress port is being used instead.
	A value of 4095 is reserved for implementation use.
	For details see ANSI/TIA-1057, Section 10.2.3.5.

MED organizationally defined set of LLDP TLVs whose transmission
	is possible on the LLDP agent of the remote device connected to this port.
	Each TLV type corresponds to a specific TIA TR41.4 MED optional TLV.
	For details see ANSI/TIA-1057, Sections 10.2.2.1.
	Values: 0=Unset, 1=CAPABILITIES, 2=EXTENDED_PD, 3=EXTENDED_PSE, 4=INVENTORY, 5=LOCATION, 6=NETWORK_POLICY.

x-enum-descriptions: Unset (0): Valid zero value for unset state
EXTENDED_PD (2): Extended PoE TLVs with PD capabilities.
EXTENDED_PSE (3): Extended PoE TLVs with PSE capabilities.

INVENTORY (4): Hardware Revision, Firmware Revision, Software Revision,
Serial Number, Manufacturer Name, Model Name, and Asset ID TLVs.
LOCATION (5): Emergency Communications System Location TLVs.

Dot3 MAC/PHY refers to the TLV (Type-Length-Value) that advertises the MAC and physical
	layer capabilities of a port. Setting this to true enables 802.3 MAC/PHY TLV advertising; the
	retrieve-asset-lldp-neighbor-xdot3 endpoint will only return data when this is enabled and
	802.3 neighbors are present.

dot3_power.description:
Dot3 power refers to the Power over Ethernet (PoE) TLV (Type-Length-Value) defined by
	IEEE 802.3. Setting this to true enables 802.3 PoE TLV advertising; the retrieve-asset-lldp-neighbor-xdot3-power
	endpoint will only return data when this is enabled and 802.3 PoE neighbors are present.

	layer capabilities of a port. Setting this to true enables 802.3 MAC/PHY TLV advertising; the
	retrieve-asset-lldp-neighbor-xdot3 endpoint will only return data when this is enabled and
	802.3 neighbors are present.

dot3_power.description:

	IEEE 802.3. Setting this to true enables 802.3 PoE TLV advertising; the retrieve-asset-lldp-neighbor-xdot3-power
	endpoint will only return data when this is enabled and 802.3 PoE neighbors are present.

nbr_detection_state.description:
List of NbrDetectionState. NbrDetectionState represents The Neighbor Unreachability Detection state for the interface.
	Fabric Engine (FE) only.

x-enum-descriptions: Unset (0): Valid zero value for unset state

REACHABLE (1): As long as there is bidirectional traffic, the neighbor state will
always report reachable. When the neighbor stops transmitting packets, a
reachability countdowntimer begins. Once the reachability timer
expires, the address will be moved to the stale state.

STALE (2): The stale state signifies that address resolution is needed. Stale entries
are kept in the ND cache for some time before being removed. Packets destined
for a neighbor in the stale state will still be forwarded by the router.
Once forwarded the neighbor unreachability detection (NUD) mechanism begins,
and the neighbor reachability state transitions to the delay state.

DELAY (3): The neighbor is no longer known to be reachable, and traffic has
recently been sent to the neighbor. Rather than probe the neighbor immediately,
however, delay sending probes for a short while in order to give upper-layer
protocols a chance to provide reachability confirmation.

PROBE (4): If there is no response after 5 seconds, the neighbor reachability state changes
to probe and three NS messages are sent for address resolution. If a response
is received from the neighbor the state changes to reachable again. If there
is no response to the three NS requests, the neighbor entry is deleted.
INVALID (5): State of the Neighbour Invalid.
UNKNOWN (6): State of the Neighbour Unknown.

INCOMPLETE (7): In the reachability state incomplete, address resolution is taking place.
The router sends an NS message to the destination address and waits for
a response. If the router receives a response, the neighbor state changes to
reachable.

LOCAL (4): Neighbour discovery based on local interface.

auto_neg_off_supported_speed_duplex_list.description:
This list contains all the speed-duplex combinations supported by the port to when
	auto-negotiation is disabled. The configured speed and duplex are managed by
	'EthernetInterface.speed; and 'EthernetInterface.duplex' when
	'EthernetInterface.autoNegotiation=False'. Maximum length: 255 characters.

auto_neg_on_supported_adv_list.description:
This list contains all the speed-duplex combinations the port is capable of advertising
	when auto-negotiation is enabled. The configured list of advertisements is managed by
	'EthernetInterface.autoAdvertisementsList' when 'EthernetInterface.autoNegotiation=True'. Maximum length: 255 characters.

auto_negotiation.description:
The auto-negotiation setting for the port.
	'configurable' means Auto-negotiation can be configured (true or false) for the port.
	'on' means auto-negotiation is supported and cannot be disabled.
	'off' means auto-negotiation is not supported.

channelization_sub_ports.description:
If channelization is supported, shows the capability of channelized sub-ports.
	For Fabric Engine (VOSS) - the partition is determined based on speed and
	channelized attributes. For a GET operation a list of partition will be returned. Maximum length: 255 characters.

channelization_support.description: Indicates whether the port supports channelization

configurable.description:
States if the port speed/duplex/autoNegotiationEnabled are configurable or not.
	For Fabric Engine for COPPER ports, this field will always be true.
	For FIBER ports, if port is not populated, it will not be configurable.
	If populated, configurable will be True, but there are certain
	scenarios for which those attributes are really configurable
	- speed is configurable only when a dual-speed optic is inserted.
	- duplex is configurable only when 25GbCX is inserted and auto-negotiation is disabled
	- auto-negotiation is configurable mostly on DACs, except the 10Gb ones
	Port description is configurable no matter if the port is populated or not

created_at.description: Specifies the date and time when the entry was created.

ddi_supported.description:
States if Digital Diagnostic Interface is supported. If is applicable only for
	FIBER ports and only if that port is populated.

default_auto_negotiation_enabled.description:
Indicates whether this port is enabled for auto negotiation or not. This represents the
	default value of auto negotiation per port. For Switch Engine plug-and-play is enabled
	when configured speed, duplex and autoNegotiationEnabled are all at their default values.
	This property is Switch Engine specific.

default_duplex.description:
This represents the default value for duplex per port. For Switch Engine plug-and-play is enabled
	when configured speed, duplex and autoNegotiationEnabled are all at their default values.
	This property is Switch Engine specific.
	Values: 0=Unset, 1=HALF_DUPLEX, 2=FULL_DUPLEX, 3=NONE, 4=AUTO.

default_speed.description:
This represents the default speed per port. For Switch Engine plug-and-play is enabled when
	configured speed, duplex and autoNegotiationEnabled are all at their default values.
	This property is Switch Engine specific.
	Values: 0=Unset, 1=SPEED_0MB, 2=SPEED_10MB, 3=SPEED_100MB, 4=SPEED_1GB, 5=SPEED_2.5GB, 6=SPEED_5GB, 7=SPEED_10GB, 8=SPEED_20GB, 9=SPEED_25GB, 10=SPEED_40GB, 11=SPEED_50GB, 12=SPEED_100GB, 13=SPEED_200GB, 14=SPEED_300GB, 15=SPEED_400GB, 16=SPEED_1GBPSAN, 17=SPEED_AUTO.

ethernet.description:
Indicates whether the port supports ethernet capability. This property is Switch Engine specific.
	Standard front panel, universal, or alternate stacking ports may have a value of true.

id.description: An auto-generated primary key identifier of the table in the UUID format defined in RFC 4122.

loopback_port.description:
Indicates that the port is allocated for loopback. Required for advanced
	feature functionality.

management_port.description: Management port for out-of-band management connection to the switch.

media_type.description:
Indicates the types of media used by the port for data transmission. This property
	is represented as a list as certain ports can support multiple media types.
	Values include: COPPER, FIBER, OTHER.

poe_max_power.description: Maximum PoE power supported by the port, in milliwatts. Valid range is 0-98000mW (0-90W, IEEE 802.3bt Type 4 maximum).

port_name.description:
Name of the interface, slot and port are required

	to ensure deterministic results, sub_port is optional.

	If the optional slot number for the management port is

	not provided on a stacked system, the slot will default

	to the master slot. Maximum length: 255 characters.

	[slot]:[port][:sub_port]

	'1:1:1'     slot=1, port=1, sub_port=1

	'12:101'    slot=12, port=101

	'1:s1'      insight port

	'ge2'       port=ge2

	'wifi1.3'   radio=1, ssid=3

	'mgmt'      oob mgmt port

	'2:mgmt'    mgmt port with optional slot

	'1:stack2'  stack port, slot=1, port=2

reserved_port.description: Reserved port for configuring advanced features. This is Fabric Engine specific.

stacking.description:
Indicates whether the port supports stacking capability.
	This property is Switch Engine specific. Dedicated stacking ports, universal,
	or alternate stacking ports may have a value of true.

updated_at.description: Specifies the date and time when the entry was last updated.

vim_port.description:
Indicates whether the port is a Virtual Infrastructure Management
	(VIM) port.

auto_neg_off_supported_speed_duplex_list.description:
This list contains all the speed-duplex combinations supported by the port to when
	auto-negotiation is disabled. The configured speed and duplex are managed by
	'EthernetInterface.speed; and 'EthernetInterface.duplex' when
	'EthernetInterface.autoNegotiation=False'. Maximum length: 255 characters.

auto_neg_on_supported_adv_list.description:
This list contains all the speed-duplex combinations the port is capable of advertising
	when auto-negotiation is enabled. The configured list of advertisements is managed by
	'EthernetInterface.autoAdvertisementsList' when 'EthernetInterface.autoNegotiation=True'. Maximum length: 255 characters.

auto_negotiation.description:
The auto-negotiation setting for the port.
	'configurable' means Auto-negotiation can be configured (true or false) for the port.
	'on' means auto-negotiation is supported and cannot be disabled.
	'off' means auto-negotiation is not supported.
x-enum-descriptions: CONFIGURABLE: Auto-negotiation can be configured (enabled or disabled) for the port.
ON: Auto-negotiation is supported and cannot be disabled.

channelization_sub_ports.description:
If channelization is supported, shows the capability of channelized sub-ports.
	For Fabric Engine (VOSS) - the partition is determined based on speed and
	channelized attributes. For a GET operation a list of partition will be returned. Maximum length: 255 characters.

channelization_support.description: Indicates whether the port supports channelization

configurable.description:
States if the port speed/duplex/autoNegotiationEnabled are configurable or not.
	For Fabric Engine for COPPER ports, this field will always be true.
	For FIBER ports, if port is not populated, it will not be configurable.
	If populated, configurable will be True, but there are certain
	scenarios for which those attributes are really configurable
	- speed is configurable only when a dual-speed optic is inserted.
	- duplex is configurable only when 25GbCX is inserted and auto-negotiation is disabled
	- auto-negotiation is configurable mostly on DACs, except the 10Gb ones
	Port description is configurable no matter if the port is populated or not

ddi_supported.description:
States if Digital Diagnostic Interface is supported. If is applicable only for
	FIBER ports and only if that port is populated.

default_auto_negotiation_enabled.description:
Indicates whether this port is enabled for auto negotiation or not. This represents the
	default value of auto negotiation per port. For Switch Engine plug-and-play is enabled
	when configured speed, duplex and autoNegotiationEnabled are all at their default values.
	This property is Switch Engine specific.

default_duplex.description:
This represents the default value for duplex per port. For Switch Engine plug-and-play is enabled
	when configured speed, duplex and autoNegotiationEnabled are all at their default values.
	This property is Switch Engine specific.
	Values: 0=Unset, 1=HALF_DUPLEX, 2=FULL_DUPLEX, 3=NONE, 4=AUTO.
x-enum-descriptions: Unset (0): Valid zero value for unset state

default_speed.description:
This represents the default speed per port. For Switch Engine plug-and-play is enabled when
	configured speed, duplex and autoNegotiationEnabled are all at their default values.
	This property is Switch Engine specific.
	Values: 0=Unset, 1=SPEED_0MB, 2=SPEED_10MB, 3=SPEED_100MB, 4=SPEED_1GB, 5=SPEED_2.5GB, 6=SPEED_5GB, 7=SPEED_10GB, 8=SPEED_20GB, 9=SPEED_25GB, 10=SPEED_40GB, 11=SPEED_50GB, 12=SPEED_100GB, 13=SPEED_200GB, 14=SPEED_300GB, 15=SPEED_400GB, 16=SPEED_1GBPSAN, 17=SPEED_AUTO.
x-enum-descriptions: Unset (0): Valid zero value for unset state
SPEED_AUTO (17): Automatically set Speed for Ethernet

ethernet.description:
Indicates whether the port supports ethernet capability. This property is Switch Engine specific.
	Standard front panel, universal, or alternate stacking ports may have a value of true.

loopback_port.description:
Indicates that the port is allocated for loopback. Required for advanced
	feature functionality.

management_port.description: Management port for out-of-band management connection to the switch.

media_type.description:
Indicates the types of media used by the port for data transmission. This property
	is represented as a list as certain ports can support multiple media types.
	Values include: COPPER, FIBER, OTHER.
x-enum-descriptions: FIBER: Port uses fiber optic media.
OTHER: Other media type or media cannot be determined. All transceiver-based cables are returned as FIBER.

poe_max_power.description: Maximum PoE power supported by the port, in milliwatts. Valid range is 0-98000mW (0-90W, IEEE 802.3bt Type 4 maximum).

port_name.description:
Name of the interface, slot and port are required

	to ensure deterministic results, sub_port is optional.

	If the optional slot number for the management port is

	not provided on a stacked system, the slot will default

	to the master slot. Maximum length: 255 characters.

	[slot]:[port][:sub_port]

	'1:1:1'     slot=1, port=1, sub_port=1

	'12:101'    slot=12, port=101

	'1:s1'      insight port

	'ge2'       port=ge2

	'wifi1.3'   radio=1, ssid=3

	'mgmt'      oob mgmt port

	'2:mgmt'    mgmt port with optional slot

	'1:stack2'  stack port, slot=1, port=2

reserved_port.description: Reserved port for configuring advanced features. This is Fabric Engine specific.

vim_port.description:
Indicates whether the port is a Virtual Infrastructure Management
	(VIM) port.

AssetPortCapabilitiesPostRequest.description: AssetPortCapabilitiesPostRequest represents the post request for AssetPortCapabilities. AssetPortCapabilities - DB Model for Port Capabilities

auto_negotiation_enabled.description:
Set to TRUE to request the interface to auto-negotiate
	transmission parameters with its peer interface.  When
	set to FALSE, the transmission parameters are specified
	manually.

channelized.description:
A value of true indicates channelization is enabled on the port.
	This parameter applies to Fabric Engine.
	For Switch Engine the partition property specifies the type of partitioning on the port.

created_at.description: Specifies the date and time when the entry was created.

debounce_timer.description:
The value of the port debounce timer in milliseconds.
	This value represents the delay link in flap detection after a link goes down.
	The range for Switch Engine is [0-5000] and the range for Fabric Engine is [0-300000].
	A value of 0 is the default on both operating systems and this indicates there is no delay in link down detection.

duplex.description:
Available transmissions type that can be set on the device when auto-negotiation is disabled
	(autoNegotiationEnabled is set to false). Capabilities can vary per port type and per platform
	(for example some platforms/ports do not offer half duplex).
	Values: 0=Unset, 1=HALF_DUPLEX, 2=FULL_DUPLEX, 3=NONE, 4=AUTO.

eee.description:
A value of true indicates the Energy Efficient Ethernet (EEE) option is enabled on the port. If enabled the port will advertise to its link partner that it is EEE capable at certain speeds.
	This setting is only applicable to Switch Engine

enabled.description: A value of true indicates the port is administratively enabled (admin up). This reflects administrative intent only and is independent of the actual operational state. Operational state is reported by oper_state in the port state model.

fec.description:
IEEE Forward Error Correction (FEC) options. The AUTO
	setting automatically configures FEC based on port
	speed and pluggable module type and is only applicable
	to Fabric Engine. This attribute can be set only for FIBER
	media type.
	Values: 0=Unset, 1=NONE, 2=CLAUSE_74, 3=CLAUSE_91_108, 4=AUTO.

flow_control.description:
Available flow control settings. Fabric Engine (VOSS) does
	not support RX_ENABLE and PFC_ENABLE values. For Fabric Engine (VOSS)
	this attribute can only be set when the boot config flag flow-control-mode
	is enabled, otherwise it should not be specified in the payload.
	Values: 0=Unset, 1=ENABLE, 2=DISABLE, 3=RX_ENABLE, 4=PFC_ENABLE.

id.description: An auto-generated primary key identifier of the table in the UUID format defined in RFC 4122.

ip_arp_inspection_trusted.description:
A value of true indicates that the interface is trusted for ARP inspection purposes.
	This parameter applies to Fabric Engine only.

jumbo_enabled.description:
A value of true indicates jumbo frames are enabled on the port and it's MTU is set to the global 'l2mtu' setting.
	This setting is only applicable to Switch Engine

name.description:
Port number (maps to the front panel port of a switch);
	also the key for the port list. Does not include the management port.

native_vlan.description:
The VLAN ID assigned to untagged frames received on this trunk port.
	This field is meaningless when the port is not a trunk port (portMode is True).
	This is Fabric Engine specific. A value of 0 indicates no native VLAN is assigned.

partition.description:
Available port partition settings. The options vary
	depending on platform and port. For a GET operation
	a single value will be returned. For a SET operation
	a single value can be configured and this list represents
	the possible values among all port types.
	For Fabric Engine (VOSS) - the partition is determined
	based on speed and channelized attributes, therefore
	this attribute is available only in a GET operation,
	but can't be configured in a SET operation. This attribute
	is available only for ports with speed 20G, 40G and 100G
	on Fabric Engine (VOSS). Values 2X50G, 3X25G, 3X10G and 3X1G
	are not supported on Fabric Engine (VOSS).

port_mode.description:
A value of True will enable the port on the current vlan to perform tagging on the incoming and outgoing traffic.
	This is Fabric Engine specific.

speed.description:
Available speed values (in Mbps/Gbps) that can be set on the device when auto-negotiation is
	disabled (autoNegotiationEnabled is set to false). Capabilities vary per port type and per platform.
	The 'AUTO' value will be returned only in GET operations for those ports that are part of a
	VIM and where the VIM Speed is automatically set. Fabric Engine (VOSS) does not support speed
	values 20G and 50G and allows this attribute to be configured only for dual speed transceivers.
	Values: 0=Unset, 1=SPEED_0MB, 2=SPEED_10MB, 3=SPEED_100MB, 4=SPEED_1GB, 5=SPEED_2.5GB, 6=SPEED_5GB, 7=SPEED_10GB, 8=SPEED_20GB, 9=SPEED_25GB, 10=SPEED_40GB, 11=SPEED_50GB, 12=SPEED_100GB, 13=SPEED_200GB, 14=SPEED_300GB, 15=SPEED_400GB, 16=SPEED_1GBPSAN, 17=SPEED_AUTO.

updated_at.description: Specifies the date and time when the entry was last updated.

IEEE Forward Error Correction (FEC) options. The AUTO
	setting automatically configures FEC based on port
	speed and pluggable module type and is only applicable
	to Fabric Engine. This attribute can be set only for FIBER
	media type.
	Values: 0=Unset, 1=NONE, 2=CLAUSE_74, 3=CLAUSE_91_108, 4=AUTO.
x-enum-descriptions: Unset (0): Valid zero value for unset state
NONE (1): Forward Error Correction (FEC) mode set None.
CLAUSE_74 (2): IEEE 802.3 Clause 74 Forward Error Correction (FEC).
CLAUSE_91_108 (3): IEEE 802.3 Clause 91 and Clause 108 Forward Error Correction (FEC).
AUTO (4): Automatically set Forward Error Correction (FEC) mode.

flow_control.description:
Available flow control settings. Fabric Engine (VOSS) does
	not support RX_ENABLE and PFC_ENABLE values. For Fabric Engine (VOSS)
	this attribute can only be set when the boot config flag flow-control-mode
	is enabled, otherwise it should not be specified in the payload.
	Values: 0=Unset, 1=ENABLE, 2=DISABLE, 3=RX_ENABLE, 4=PFC_ENABLE.
x-enum-descriptions: Unset (0): Valid zero value for unset state
ENABLE (1): Enables Flow Control settings on the port.
DISABLE (2): Disables Flow Control settings on the port.
RX_ENABLE (3): Enable Rx Flow Control settings on the port.
PFC_ENABLE (4): Enable Priority Flow Control settings on the port.

ip_arp_inspection_trusted.description:
A value of true indicates that the interface is trusted for ARP inspection purposes.
	This parameter applies to Fabric Engine only.

jumbo_enabled.description:
A value of true indicates jumbo frames are enabled on the port and it's MTU is set to the global 'l2mtu' setting.
	This setting is only applicable to Switch Engine

name.description:
Port number (maps to the front panel port of a switch);
	also the key for the port list. Does not include the management port.

native_vlan.description:
The VLAN ID assigned to untagged frames received on this trunk port.
	This field is meaningless when the port is not a trunk port (portMode is True).
	This is Fabric Engine specific. A value of 0 indicates no native VLAN is assigned.

partition.description:
Available port partition settings. The options vary
	depending on platform and port. For a GET operation
	a single value will be returned. For a SET operation
	a single value can be configured and this list represents
	the possible values among all port types.
	For Fabric Engine (VOSS) - the partition is determined
	based on speed and channelized attributes, therefore
	this attribute is available only in a GET operation,
	but can't be configured in a SET operation. This attribute
	is available only for ports with speed 20G, 40G and 100G
	on Fabric Engine (VOSS). Values 2X50G, 3X25G, 3X10G and 3X1G
	are not supported on Fabric Engine (VOSS).
x-enum-descriptions: Unset (0): Valid zero value for unset state

1X100G (1): Partitioning a 100G port into a single 100G port
(applies only to switches with 100G port(s)).

1X40G (2): Partitioning a 40G port into a single 40G port
(applies only to switches with 40G port(s)).
1X20G (3): Partitioning a 20G port into a single 20G port.

port_mode.description:
A value of True will enable the port on the current vlan to perform tagging on the incoming and outgoing traffic.
	This is Fabric Engine specific.

speed.description:
Available speed values (in Mbps/Gbps) that can be set on the device when auto-negotiation is
	disabled (autoNegotiationEnabled is set to false). Capabilities vary per port type and per platform.
	The 'AUTO' value will be returned only in GET operations for those ports that are part of a
	VIM and where the VIM Speed is automatically set. Fabric Engine (VOSS) does not support speed
	values 20G and 50G and allows this attribute to be configured only for dual speed transceivers.
	Values: 0=Unset, 1=SPEED_0MB, 2=SPEED_10MB, 3=SPEED_100MB, 4=SPEED_1GB, 5=SPEED_2.5GB, 6=SPEED_5GB, 7=SPEED_10GB, 8=SPEED_20GB, 9=SPEED_25GB, 10=SPEED_40GB, 11=SPEED_50GB, 12=SPEED_100GB, 13=SPEED_200GB, 14=SPEED_300GB, 15=SPEED_400GB, 16=SPEED_1GBPSAN, 17=SPEED_AUTO.
x-enum-descriptions: Unset (0): Valid zero value for unset state
SPEED_AUTO (17): Automatically set Speed for Ethernet

civic_address.description:
Civic based location information.
	Switch Engine uses a flexible format but has a minimum
	requirement of 6 bytes.
	Fabric Engine uses civic address LCI data format.
	A valid request for Fabric Engine should always start with country-code label
	followed by 2 characters for the country code. Country-code is not
	enough for setting the civic address, so another eligible label should
	also be set.
	All eligible labels that can be set in a civic address are:
	additional-code, additional-information, apartment, block, building,
	city, city-district, county, floor, house-number, house-number-suffix,
	landmark, leading-street-direction, name, place-type, pobox,
	postal-community-name, postal-zip-code, room-number, state, street,
	street-suffix, trailing-street-suffix.

	is recommended that values are assigned contiguously
	starting from 1.  The value for each interface sub-layer
	must remain constant at least from one re-initialization of
	the entity's network management system to the next reinitialization.

local_name.description:
The textual name of the interface as assigned by the local device;
	suitable for use in commands entered at the device's console.
	Native/CLI-facing format, as opposed to 'name' which is the
	deterministic colon-separated [slot]:[port][:sub_port] identifier.

mac_address.description:
Assigns a MAC address to the Ethernet interface.  If not
	specified, the corresponding operational state leaf is
	expected to show the system-assigned MAC address.

name.description:
Port number (maps to the front panel port of a switch);
	also the key for the port list. Does not include the management port.

oper_duplex.description: Indicate this port's current duplex value.

oper_speed.description:
Indicate this port's current speed value. Fabric Engine (VOSS) does not support speed
	values 20G and 50G.
	Values: 0=Unset, 1=SPEED_0MB, 2=SPEED_10MB, 3=SPEED_100MB, 4=SPEED_1GB, 5=SPEED_2.5GB, 6=SPEED_5GB, 7=SPEED_10GB, 8=SPEED_20GB, 9=SPEED_25GB, 10=SPEED_40GB, 11=SPEED_50GB, 12=SPEED_100GB, 13=SPEED_200GB, 14=SPEED_300GB, 15=SPEED_400GB, 16=SPEED_1GBPSAN, 17=SPEED_AUTO.

oper_state.description:
The current operational state of the interface.  The
	testing state indicates that no operational packets can
	be passed.  If admin state is down then oper state
	should be down. If admin state is changed to up
	then oper state should change to up and the interface is
	ready to transmit and receive network traffic. It should
	change to dormant if the interface is waiting for
	external actions (such as a serial line waiting for an
	incoming connection). It should remain in the down state
	if and only if there is a fault that prevents it from going
	to the up state; It should remain in the notPresent
	state if the interface has missing (typically, hardware)
	components.
	Values: 0=Unset, 1=UP, 2=DOWN, 3=TESTING, 4=UNKNOWN, 5=DORMANT, 6=NOT_PRESENT, 7=LOWER_LAYER_DOWN.

operation_mode.description: Operation Mode. Values: unknown, auto, AP, ACCESS, BACKHAUL, SENSOR, BRIDGE, DUAL, WAN, TRUNK. An empty string indicates the mode is not configured.

silkscreen_name.description:
The numbering printed on the physical silkscreen of the switch chassis
	next to the port. Not guaranteed unique — multiple ports (e.g. across
	stack members) can report the same value.

slpp_status.description:
The SLPP safe guard status for the port.
	SLPP guard state is set to MONITORING if the port is operational UP and
	SLPP guard is enabled on that port. The state is set to BLOCKING when the
	port is disabled by SLPP guard. If SLPP is not enabled on the port, the state
	is set to NONE.
	Values: 0=Unset, 1=BLOCKING, 2=MONITORING, 3=NONE.

oper_speed.description:

	values 20G and 50G.
	Values: 0=Unset, 1=SPEED_0MB, 2=SPEED_10MB, 3=SPEED_100MB, 4=SPEED_1GB, 5=SPEED_2.5GB, 6=SPEED_5GB, 7=SPEED_10GB, 8=SPEED_20GB, 9=SPEED_25GB, 10=SPEED_40GB, 11=SPEED_50GB, 12=SPEED_100GB, 13=SPEED_200GB, 14=SPEED_300GB, 15=SPEED_400GB, 16=SPEED_1GBPSAN, 17=SPEED_AUTO.
x-enum-descriptions: Unset (0): Valid zero value for unset state
SPEED_AUTO (17): Automatically set Speed for Ethernet

oper_state.description:
The current operational state of the interface.  The
	testing state indicates that no operational packets can
	be passed.  If admin state is down then oper state
	should be down. If admin state is changed to up
	then oper state should change to up and the interface is
	ready to transmit and receive network traffic. It should
	change to dormant if the interface is waiting for
	external actions (such as a serial line waiting for an
	incoming connection). It should remain in the down state
	if and only if there is a fault that prevents it from going
	to the up state; It should remain in the notPresent
	state if the interface has missing (typically, hardware)
	components.
	Values: 0=Unset, 1=UP, 2=DOWN, 3=TESTING, 4=UNKNOWN, 5=DORMANT, 6=NOT_PRESENT, 7=LOWER_LAYER_DOWN.

DOWN (2): The interface does not pass any packets.

TESTING (3): In some test mode. No operational packets can
be passed.
UNKNOWN (4): Status cannot be determined for some reason.
DORMANT (5): Waiting for some external event.
NOT_PRESENT (6): Some component (typically hardware) is missing.
LOWER_LAYER_DOWN (7): Down due to state of lower-layer interface(s).

	SLPP guard state is set to MONITORING if the port is operational UP and
	SLPP guard is enabled on that port. The state is set to BLOCKING when the
	port is disabled by SLPP guard. If SLPP is not enabled on the port, the state
	is set to NONE.

	CP & IO and SF Card.

mac_address_capacity.description: MAC address capacity in number of addresses supported by this slot.

model_name.description: Device model name.

node_state.description:
Node state - Switch Engine (EXOS) only. Configuration commands are
	prevented when the stack's backup node is in BACKUP state.
	Administrative failover operations are prevented when the stack's backup
	node is in BACKUP or BACKUP_CONFIG_SYNCED states. It is safe to perform
	a failover when the stack's backup node is in BACKUP_IN_SYNC state.

num_ports.description: The total number of ports currently installed in the chassis.

operation_status.description:
Device operational status. DOWN is applicable to both Fabric Engine and
	Switch Engine. UP, TESTING, UNKNOWN, DORMANT, UP_MASTER, UP_DORMANT and
	UP_WARMSTANDBY are applicable to Fabric Engine. The others are
	applicable to Switch Engine.

sys_boot_time.description:
Epoch seconds (UTC) the device last booted. For wired devices,
	derived from sys-up-time at ingest; for wireless APs, sourced
	directly from the device-reported boot epoch.

sys_build_time.description:
System build time as a date-time string. Format varies by OS
	(e.g., VOSS: 'Tue/Nov/25/14:17:39/EST/2025', EXOS: 'Fri Mar 28 10:37:33 PM UTC 2025').

sys_up_time.description:
The time (in hundredths of a second) since the network
	management portion of the system was last re-initialized.

updated_at.description: Specifies the date and time when the entry was last updated.

	is configured; consumers should treat an empty string as equivalent to
	null/absent. Maximum length: 255 characters.

primary_vlan.description:
Primary VLAN id for this SPBM instance. A value of 0 is a sentinel
	meaning there is no primary VLAN because the vlans attribute contains fewer
	than 2 VLANs; consumers should treat 0 as equivalent to null/absent.
	When vlans contains exactly 2 VLANs, this field identifies which of the two
	is the primary VLAN.

smlt_bmac.description:
SMLT backbone MAC address used for multi-homing. An empty string
	indicates that no SMLT peer is configured; consumers should treat an
	empty string as equivalent to null/absent.

stp_multi_homing.description: A value of True indicates Fabric Multi-Homing is enabled.

updated_at.description: Specifies the date and time when the entry was last updated.

vlans.description:
ISIS SPBM instance data VLANs. There can be at most 2 VLANs set.
	VLAN numbers are encoded as strings (e.g., ["4051", "4052"]);
	consumers must cast to integer for numeric comparisons.
	When exactly 2 VLANs are present, see primary-vlan to determine
	which is the primary.

	On Fabric Engine (VOSS), actions are not supported for broadcast packets.

x-enum-descriptions: Unset (0): Valid zero value for unset state

the switch drops packets for the controlled traffic types.
SHUTDOWN (2): When the storm control level is exceeded, the switch shuts down the interface.
TRAP (3): When the storm control level is exceeded, the switch sends a trap to the SNMP manager.
LOG (4): When the storm control level is exceeded, the switch logs to system log file.

	On Fabric Engine (VOSS), actions are not supported for broadcast packets.

x-enum-descriptions: Unset (0): Valid zero value for unset state

the switch drops packets for the controlled traffic types.
SHUTDOWN (2): When the storm control level is exceeded, the switch shuts down the interface.
TRAP (3): When the storm control level is exceeded, the switch sends a trap to the SNMP manager.
LOG (4): When the storm control level is exceeded, the switch logs to system log file.

protocol.description: List of Protocol. Protocol represents STP Protocol.

x-enum-descriptions: Unset (0): Valid zero value for unset state

STP (1): Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) is the original STP protocol that
prevents redundant paths and bridging loops in a network topology.
It creates a single spanning tree for the entire network.

RSTP (2): An enhanced version of STP that uses a negotiation mechanism to
synchronize topology changes between switches. It doesn't use
timers like the original STP, which results in faster re-convergence
times.

MSTP (3): MSTP is an extension to Rapid Spanning Tree Protocol (RSTP).
Multiple Spanning Tree Protocol (MSTP) is a protocol that creates
multiple spanning trees (instances) for each Virtual LAN (VLAN) on
a single physical network. This allows for each VLAN to have a configured
root bridge and forwarding topology.
